method_card.title: Normal Distribution and Standardising Data
method_card.content:
The Normal distribution is a symmetric, bell-shaped curve. The mean, median and mode are all equal and sit at the centre. The curve tapers off symmetrically in both directions — tails that never quite touch the axis.

You need to recall three key results without a z-table:

  • Approximately 68% of data lies within 1 standard deviation of the mean — between \(\mu - \sigma\) and \(\mu + \sigma\).
  • Approximately 95% of data lies within 2 standard deviations of the mean.
  • Values more than 3 standard deviations from the mean are very unusual.

No calculations beyond these three results are expected on the specification. You will not need a full z-table.

Standardising data converts a raw score into a standardised score (sometimes called a z-score) so that you can compare values from different distributions. The formula will always be given in the question: $$z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$$

A higher standardised score means the value is further above its group’s mean. A negative z-score means the value is below the mean. To decide “which student did better relative to their group?” — calculate both z-scores and compare.
steps: Identify the mean (\(\mu\)) and standard deviation (\(\sigma\)) of the distribution
For the 68/95 results: calculate \(\mu \pm \sigma\) and \(\mu \pm 2\sigma\) to find the boundary values
For standardising: substitute \(x\), \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\) into the given formula \(z = (x - \mu) / \sigma\)
Interpret the z-score: positive means above average, negative means below average
To compare two students from different groups, calculate both z-scores and choose the higher one

exam_context.marks: 3 to 5 marks; Higher tier only; standardising questions often ask for calculation (2 marks) plus comparison (1–2 marks)
exam_context.frequency: Appears regularly on Higher tier papers; the 68/95 results and standardising are the key testable skills

worked_examples.question: The heights of adult men in a country are Normally distributed with mean 175 cm and standard deviation 8 cm. Between which two heights do approximately 95% of men fall?

steps.label: Step 1 — Recall the 95% result
steps.content: Approximately 95% of data in a Normal distribution lies within 2 standard deviations of the mean.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Approximately 95% of men have heights between 159 cm and 191 cm.

worked_examples.question: Exam scores in Class A are Normally distributed with mean 60 and standard deviation 10. Exam scores in Class B are Normally distributed with mean 50 and standard deviation 5. Student X scored 75 in Class A. Student Y scored 60 in Class B. The standardising formula z = (x − mean) / standard deviation is given. Which student performed better relative to their class?

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Student Y performed better relative to their class (z = 2.0 vs z = 1.5). Although Student X scored a higher raw mark, Student Y was further above their class average in terms of standard deviations.

worked_examples.question: Reaction times (ms) for a driving simulator are Normally distributed with mean 240 ms and standard deviation 30 ms. A safety threshold is set at 3 standard deviations above the mean. A researcher records a reaction time of 340 ms. Using z = (x − mean) / SD (given), calculate the z-score and state whether 340 ms is within the safety threshold.

steps.label: Step 2 — Compare to the threshold
steps.content: The safety threshold is 3 standard deviations above the mean. The z-score is 3.33, which exceeds 3.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The z-score is approximately 3.33. This exceeds the 3 standard deviation threshold, so a reaction time of 340 ms is very unusual and outside the safety threshold. Values more than 3 standard deviations from the mean are considered very unusual in a Normal distribution.

bronze.display: A Normal distribution has mean 50 and standard deviation 6. What percentage of data lies within 1 standard deviation of the mean?

misconceptions.message: Approximately 68% of data in a Normal distribution lies within 1 standard deviation of the mean. This is a key result to recall.

bronze.display: A Normal distribution has mean 100 and standard deviation 15. Between which two values does approximately 95% of the data lie?
A Normal distribution has mean 200 and standard deviation 20. Is a value of 270 unusual? Select the best reason.
options: Yes — 270 is 3.5 standard deviations above the mean, which is more than 3 and therefore very unusual
No — 270 is within 2 standard deviations of the mean
No — any value in a Normal distribution is possible, so none are unusual
Yes — 270 is above the mean, and values above the mean are always unusual

misconceptions.message: z = (270 - 200) / 20 = 3.5. Values more than 3 standard deviations from the mean are considered very unusual.

bronze.display: Standardise a score of 78 from a distribution with mean 70 and standard deviation 4. The formula z = (x − mean) / SD is given. What is the z-score?
Which of the following best describes the shape of a Normal distribution?
options: Symmetric bell-shaped curve with mean = median = mode
Skewed to the right with a long upper tail
Uniform rectangle where all values are equally likely
J-shaped curve falling from left to right

misconceptions.message: The Normal distribution is symmetric and bell-shaped. Mean, median and mode are all equal and at the centre.

bronze.display: A Normal distribution has mean 40 and standard deviation 5. What is the value that is exactly 1 standard deviation above the mean?

misconceptions.message: 1 SD above the mean = mean + SD = 40 + 5 = 45.

bronze.display: The lengths of fish caught in a lake are Normally distributed with mean 32 cm and standard deviation 4 cm. Approximately what percentage of fish are longer than 40 cm?

misconceptions.message: 40 cm = mean + 2 SD (32 + 8 = 40). Approximately 95% of fish lie between mean ± 2 SD. So 5% lie outside this range. By symmetry, half of that (2.5%) is above 40 cm.

bronze.display: A standardised score (z-score) is −1.5. What does the negative sign tell you about the original value?
options: The original value is below the mean of the distribution
The original value is above the mean of the distribution
The original value is equal to the mean
The original value is impossible in a Normal distribution

misconceptions.message: A negative z-score means x is below the mean (x − mean is negative). A positive z-score means x is above the mean.

silver.display: Test scores are Normally distributed with mean 55 and standard deviation 8. Using z = (x − mean) / SD (given), standardise a score of 47. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

misconceptions.message: z = (47 - 55) / 8 = -8 / 8 = -1. The negative sign is important — 47 is below the mean.

silver.display: Heights of plants in Greenhouse A are Normally distributed: mean 35 cm, SD 4 cm. Approximately how many of 200 plants would you expect to be between 27 cm and 43 cm tall?

misconceptions.message: 27 = 35 - 2(4) and 43 = 35 + 2(4). So this is the mean ± 2 SD range. 95% of plants fall here. 0.95 × 200 = 190.

silver.display: Student P scored 82 in a test where mean = 75, SD = 7. Student Q scored 71 in a test where mean = 60, SD = 5. The formula z = (x − mean) / SD is given. Who performed better relative to their group?
options: Student Q — z = 2.2 compared to Student P's z = 1.0
Student P — their raw score is higher
Student P — z = 1.0 compared to Student Q's z = 2.2
Both students performed equally because both scored above the mean

misconceptions.message: z_P = (82 - 75) / 7 = 1.0. z_Q = (71 - 60) / 5 = 2.2. Student Q has a higher z-score, so performed better relative to their group despite having a lower raw mark.

silver.display: A Normal distribution has mean 120 and standard deviation 12. What proportion of data lies below 96?

misconceptions.message: 96 = 120 - 2(12) = mean - 2 SD. 95% lies within 2 SD, so 5% lies outside. By symmetry, 2.5% lies below 96.

silver.display: Why can you not use the Normal distribution model to find P(X = exactly 175 cm) for a continuous variable?
options: For continuous data, probability is only defined for a range of values, not a single point
The Normal distribution only applies to discrete data
The mean must equal 175 for any probability to exist
The Normal distribution cannot model human heights

misconceptions.message: The Normal distribution is for continuous data. For continuous variables, the probability of any exact single value is 0 — only ranges have non-zero probability.

silver.display: Two factories produce bolts. Factory A: Normally distributed diameters, mean 10 mm, SD 0.2 mm. Factory B: mean 10 mm, SD 0.05 mm. Which factory produces more consistent bolts?
options: Factory B — smaller standard deviation means diameters are more tightly clustered around 10 mm
Factory A — larger standard deviation means more bolts are produced
Both are equally consistent because they have the same mean
Factory A — a larger standard deviation means the Normal distribution is wider and more accurate

misconceptions.message: Smaller SD = less spread = more consistent. Factory B's SD (0.05 mm) is much smaller, so its bolt diameters vary less from the target 10 mm.

gold.display: Three students sit different tests. Student A: score 88, class mean 80, class SD 10. Student B: score 65, class mean 50, class SD 10. Student C: score 72, class mean 68, class SD 2. The standardising formula z = (x − mean) / SD is given. Rank the three students from best to worst relative to their class.
options: A, B, C in raw score order

gold.display: A machine fills bags of flour. Bag weights are Normally distributed with mean 500 g and SD 8 g. Quality control rejects bags outside mean ± 2 SD. What is the minimum acceptable weight?
Scores on a physics test are Normally distributed: mean 62, SD 9. Using z = (x − mean) / SD (given), find the z-score for a student who scored 53. Interpret whether this is an unusual score.
options: z = −1; not unusual — within 1 SD of the mean, so about 68% of students score in this range
z = −1; unusual — below-average scores are always considered unusual
z = 1; not unusual — positive z-scores are within the expected range
z = −9; very unusual — more than 3 SD from the mean

misconceptions.message: z = (53 - 62) / 9 = -9/9 = -1. This is within 1 SD of the mean, which is not unusual (about 68% of scores fall within ±1 SD of the mean).

gold.display: A Normal distribution has mean 200 and SD 25. How many standard deviations is a value of 162.5 from the mean? Give your answer as a decimal.

misconceptions.message: z = (162.5 - 200) / 25 = -37.5 / 25 = -1.5. The value is 1.5 standard deviations below the mean.

gold.display: An athlete's sprint times are Normally distributed: mean 11.2 s, SD 0.3 s. The athlete records a time of 10.3 s. Using the 3 SD rule, explain whether this time is very unusual.
options: Yes — 10.3 s is 3 standard deviations below the mean (z = −3), which is considered very unusual
No — 10.3 s is within 2 standard deviations, so it is not unusual
Yes — any time below the mean is considered very unusual
No — the 3 SD rule only applies to values above the mean

misconceptions.message: z = (10.3 - 11.2) / 0.3 = -0.9 / 0.3 = -3. Exactly 3 standard deviations from the mean — values at or beyond ±3 SD are very unusual in a Normal distribution.
